column1: The original cirth writing "Certhas Daeron" was created by the elf Daeron, the minstrel of king Thingol of Doriath and was later expanded into what was known as the Angerthas Daeron. Although the Cirth were later largely replaced by the Tengwar (which were enhanced and brought by Fëanor), they were adopted by Dwarves to write down their Khuzdul language (Angerthas Moria and Angerthas Erebor) because their straight lines were better suited to carving than the curved strokes of the Tengwar.   -------   Note: some pronunciations vary by Kindred, hence the phonetical pronounciation is noted for both Eastern Dwarrow Kindreds (Blacklocks, Ironfists, Stiffbeards and Stonefoots), Central* Kindred (Longbeards) and for the Western Dwarrow Kindreds (Broadbeams and Firebeards).  As you'll notice most consonants are the same (apart from "r" , "h", "gh" and "j"), the different pronounciation is mainly in the vowels.  *The Western Dwarrow Kindreds use identical consonants (except "nd") as those seen with the Longbeards.   The Eastern pronounciation is likely the one considered most true to the words of Mahal, due to the contact with the Elves in the West by the Western and Central Dwarrow Kindreds.  --- in the year 3019 TA Angerthas Moria and Angerthas Erebor are both used by the Dwarves of the West (although Moria style is by far the most used) - It is likely the Dwarves of the East use Angerthas Moria, though it is possible they have a different writing form altogether.
